newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real rises 0.09 pct on dollar inflows.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real rises 0.09 pct on dollar inflows.

text.p: Brazil's real rose 0.09 percent to close at 1.0246 real per dollar on dollar inflows in the commercial foreign exchange market, dealers said.
In the morning, the Central Bank took advantage of calm trading due to the Columbus Day holiday in the United States to set a new real-dollar mini-band, dealers said.
The Central Bank fixed the mini-band between 1.0245 and 1.0295 reais per greenback through a buy/sell auction.
The previous real mini-band was set on Oct 9 between 1.0235 and 1.0285 per dollar.
Later, the Central Bank bought dollars at 1.0245 real per greenback to drain excess dollars from the market.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Monday surplus of $50 million. On Friday, the dollar flows posted a $67.5 million surplus.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real dropped 0.08 percent to end at 1.0302 per dollar following the new mini-band.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed down 0.19 percent at 1.047 real per greenback.
